spec_trace.primary_anchor: 2.3.13.12 Local Account, Principal, Access Space, and Protected Resource Authority
supporting_anchors: 4.9 Role Execution Identity and Profile Naming
spec_trace.roadmap_pointer: Kernel reset brief Week 6 Account, Principal, Resource Authority, Access Space, and Persona/CRM Layers; Phase A.

original_intent_carried_forward: Principal is the kernel-level auditable subject for events, write boxes, CRDT identity, sessions, sandboxes, capabilities, and Flight Recorder attribution.
Handshake-spawned agents inherit only the intersection of parent authority and spawn grant.
PostgreSQL Row-Level Security is the fail-closed data boundary.
RootOperator break-glass prevents a policy error from permanently bricking an installation.
Existing KERNEL-001/002/003 authority data receives replay-safe ownership backfill.
new_scope_added: LocalAccount credentials, account lifecycle, and authenticated sessions on a shared PC.
Stable owner/account/principal/session/Space linkage on protected database resources.
Windows-bound secret/key storage and honest application-isolation boundary.
Future external identity binding seam without provider-specific integration.
superseded_draft_assumptions: The product is not designed only for a solo operator.
A spawned agent keeps its own Principal identity and delegation chain; it does not collapse to the human principal_id.
Principal is auditable actor identity, not the login credential row and not the complete authorization policy.
A local config assertion alone is insufficient for break-glass; recovery requires strong re-authentication, narrow scope, expiry, and immutable audit.
Runtime PostgreSQL roles must not own protected tables or bypass FORCE RLS.

naming_contract.LocalAccount: credential holder on one Handshake installation
naming_contract.AuthenticatedSession: bounded login session pinned to LocalAccount, Principal, and AccessSpace
naming_contract.AccountRole: installation Owner/Admin/Member authority, separate from content read access
naming_contract.AccessSpace: selected authorized work context; defined fully by WP-KERNEL-007
naming_contract.Persona: preferences and personalization; defined fully by WP-KERNEL-008
naming_contract.WorkProfile: model routing, budgets, autonomy, and execution policy

scope.intent: Establish trustworthy local login identity, auditable Principal identity, session attribution, account administration, and the PostgreSQL ownership/RLS substrate that every later resource grant, visitor/MCP gate, Persona, shared workspace, and SaaS link uses.
in_scope: UUID v7 identifiers and enums for LocalAccount, AuthenticatedSession, Principal, PrincipalKind, AccountRole, delegation, and revocation epochs.
LocalAccount PostgreSQL schema, username normalization, password-verifier metadata, account status, last-login/security timestamps, and lifecycle operations.
Memory-hard password hashing with versioned parameters, rate-limited login, logout/lock/session renewal, password change, session revocation, and disabled-account denial.
First-run installation Owner ceremony and explicit bootstrap invariants.
Principal kinds for human account, local/remote model, spawned agent, MCP client, service identity, visitor pass, and break-glass operator.
AccountRole-to-administrative-capability mapping without blanket private-content read.
AuthorityContext derived server-side and pinned to each transaction/session.
Spawned-agent capability and ResourceGrant intersection plus full delegation-chain attribution.

KernelActor to PrincipalRef migration across EventLedger, Flight Recorder, WriteBox, CRDT, Sandbox, ValidationRunner, PromotionGate, ArtifactStore, memory, search/index, and diagnostics records touched by Kernel V1.
Owner/account/principal/session columns and indexes on existing authority-bearing tables.
RLS policies with FORCE RLS, runtime-role tripwires, transaction-local context, fail-closed missing context, and constant-shape denial.
Replay-safe backfill, migration rollback/repair, orphan quarantine, and audit receipts.
RootOperator break-glass with protected recovery material, strong re-authentication, reason, narrow scope, expiry, and immutable event trail.
Windows Data Protection API or equivalent product-managed vault seam for session/credential-adjacent secrets and account keys.
Backend APIs plus native login, account switch, lock, and account-administration UI with Argus identifiers.
Flight Recorder/EventLedger login, account, session, role, delegation, and break-glass events.
Real PostgreSQL, negative authorization, concurrent-session, restart, migration, UserManual, and Argus verification.
out_of_scope: AccessSpace and ResourceGrant CRUD/evaluation beyond the minimum foreign-key/context seam; WP-KERNEL-007 owns them.
Visitor-pass issuance, MCP fingerprinting, per-tool scrutiny, and ResourceBroker; WP-KERNEL-007 owns them.
Persona, CRM, preference learning, client associations, and FEMS personalization; WP-KERNEL-008 owns them.
Remote SaaS implementation, federation, SSO, billing, and public cloud operations.

mandatory_negative_scenarios: runtime database role attempts owner/BYPASSRLS path
spawned agent requests broader authority than parent

selected_patterns: PostgreSQL FORCE RLS with non-owner runtime role
stable actor/resource tuples and delegation chains
rejected_patterns: provider chat identity as Handshake identity

activation_acceptance: Refinement locks all schemas, enum values, migrations, RLS policy templates, DB roles, transaction context, credential/session algorithms, break-glass procedure, and threat model.
Refinement maps every existing authority table and failure path to ownership/session attribution and backfill behavior.
Refinement carries the v02.202 research basis, rejected options, risks, mitigations, validation plan, and HBR-PRIV matrix.
Official packet adopts the complete pre-created MT index without silent deletion; changes are explicit and traceable.
A new WP activation signature is obtained; the v02.202 spec signature is not reused.

risks_and_hardening.failure_scenario: policy denies legitimate owner or table-owning runtime bypasses policies
risks_and_hardening.hardening: FORCE RLS, non-owner runtime role, migration tripwire, break-glass test, explicit positive/negative policy matrix

risks_and_hardening.failure_scenario: offline password cracking, session fixation, stale token after password change
risks_and_hardening.hardening: memory-hard verifier, rate limiting, session rotation, revocation epoch, OS vault, security events

risks_and_hardening.failure_scenario: legacy rows become visible to the wrong account
risks_and_hardening.hardening: deterministic classification, ambiguous-row quarantine, dry-run report, rollback and replay test

risks_and_hardening.failure_scenario: child model inherits all owner access or loses attribution
risks_and_hardening.hardening: intersection semantics, task resource set, delegation chain, bounded lease, concurrent revoke test

risks_and_hardening.failure_scenario: coworker admin can read private porn-production resources
risks_and_hardening.hardening: separate AccountRole from ResourceGrant, no blanket read, audited narrow break-glass only

microtasks.adoption_rule: Activation Manager must compare refinement/packet scope to every pre-created MT, preserve each original obligation, record any split/merge/supersession, validate the DAG, and activate no more than one MT at a time.

minimum_controls: No product implementation may begin from this stub or its inactive MTs.
Refinement must prove login identity, Principal attribution, authorization context, RLS, revocation, migration, and recovery as separate boundaries.
Same-PC different-account and same-project different-resource privacy are mandatory design scenarios.
